summary:
Karachay-Cherkessia falls within the North Caucasus regional exception identified by the UK Home Office CPIN (June 2025) and named in Western don't-travel guidance for the Caucasus zone. The North Caucasus SOS assessment of no safe life for LGBTIQ+ people in the region applies here. The security-and-custom enforcement logic—informal detention, family exposure, violence unmediated by legal process—is the operative risk for a discovered visitor.

No Chechnya-style documented purge infrastructure or specific special-permission entry regime is identified for Karachay-Cherkessia. Approximately 0.07 below the national score of 0.12. Equal to Kabardino-Balkaria and North Ossetia in the broader North Caucasus bloc; above Dagestan and Ingushetia (0.04), which carry the explicit special-access designation.

sources.summary: Interview on the Human Rights House Foundation site with David Isteev of North Caucasus SOS on protecting LGBTIQ+ people in the North Caucasus: 'there is no safe life for LGBTIQ+ people in the North Caucasus, and even private existence can trigger violence, detention, or forced return to families'; the organisation coordinates roughly 34 evacuations a year from exile, with security consultations, legal and psychological support and temporary solutions for those who stay.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (GOV.UK returned only a cookie-consent shell); the underlying document is the UK Home Office Country Policy and Information Note on sexual orientation and gender identity/expression (June 2025), which concludes that LGBT+ people form a particular social group but that, while sexual minorities generally do not face a real risk of state persecution in Russia, those in the North Caucasus, trans people and publicly active LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution.

tangentialFactors: The informal-enforcement pattern documented for the zone - round-ups, detention, family exposure, violence unmediated by legal process - was first recorded against gay men and LGBTIQ+ people generally rather than trans people specifically; the same security-and-custom logic operates on any discovered queer visitor, trans or not.
outOfScopeNotes: The Western don't-travel designation for the North Caucasus zone is driven largely by general armed-conflict and security risk that affects all travellers; the trans-relevant content is the LGBT-specific exception drawn by the UK Home Office note, not the blanket advisory level.
